name: Mauritius
sources: World Bank figures in this file were read off IndexMundi's republication of the WDI series named, because api.worldbank.org and data.worldbank.org returned a WAF block page to this session throughout. The full provenance caveat is written out once, in madagascar.json, and applies here identically.

GDP $2.65bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series MUS, 1990 = 2,653,480,000. On 1.06m people that is about $2,505 a head - seven times Madagascar's, four hundred kilometres away, and the highest income on this branch by a wide margin.
Population 1.06m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MUS, 1990 = 1,058,775.

TFP trend 0.013: the highest on this branch and it is earned rather than flattering. Mauritius in 1990 is the middle of the export-processing-zone boom - real GDP growing around 6-7% a year since 1983, unemployment down from roughly 20% at the start of the decade to under 3%, and the economy moved from a sugar monoculture to knitwear and textiles for the European market under the Lome and Multi-Fibre arrangements. Set level with the roster's better East Asian performers rather than with its African ones, because this is what Mauritius actually was: the counter-example that the development literature has been arguing about ever since Meade predicted in 1961 that the island had no prospects at all. What it is NOT is permanent - the MFA quotas that carried the textile sector were scheduled to expire, and they did, in 2005.

Inflation 13.5%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, series MUS, 1990 = 13.49. High for a country doing this well, and it is the boom itself: wage pressure from full employment plus an imported inflation from a rupee the Bank of Mauritius had let slide to keep the EPZ competitive.

Interest rate 18%: World Bank FR.INR.LEND, series MUS, 1990 = 18.00, the commercial bank lending rate, the same substitution the rest of the roster makes for the policy rate. Real rate +4.5 points. The loader's coupled check reads 0.025 - (0.18 - 0.135) = -0.020.
Revenue 22.5% of GDP: World Bank GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS, series MUS, 1990 = 22.53, revenue excluding grants.

Military 0.35% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, series MUS, 1990 = 0.346. Rounded to 0.003 in the file's fraction-of-1 units. THE LOWEST MILITARY BURDEN IN THE ENTIRE ROSTER, and it is a constitutional fact rather than a rounding: Mauritius has no army. It has never had one. What the 0.35% buys is the Special Mobile Force and the National Coast Guard, both branches of the police, together about 1,300 men.

Investment 7% state / 23% private, summing to 30% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, series MUS, 1990 = 30.21, gross capital formation. The 7/23 split is APPORTIONED and sums to the sourced total; it is put heavily toward the private side because that is where the investment was - the EPZ factories were built by Franco-Mauritian sugar capital and Hong Kong partners, not by the state.

Debt 35.4% of GDP: World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, series MUS, 1990 = 35.44, external debt stocks as a share of GNI. Mauritius had gone to the IMF three times between 1979 and 1985 and had come out; by 1990 it was the rare adjustment programme everybody could point at.

Stability 76 and authoritarianism 0.12: a Westminster parliamentary democracy that has never had a coup, never had a state of emergency it did not lift, and has changed government at the ballot box repeatedly - Ramgoolam out in 1982, Jugnauth's MSM/Labour/PMSD alliance winning the general election of 30 August 1987, and the split with Berenger's MMM that was already running by 1990. Stability set above Spain's 70 and just above India's, on a record of institutional continuity that the size of the place makes easier rather than less real. Authoritarianism 0.12 is level with Spain's 0.13.

Separatism 0.02: Rodrigues, 560km east, culturally Creole rather than Indo-Mauritian, and represented by the Organisation du Peuple de Rodrigues, which wanted autonomy and got it in 2002. Not a secessionist movement in 1990 and never an armed one. Near the roster's floor.

Military strength 0.2: THE LOWEST INDEX IN THE ROSTER, below Bahrain's 0.6 and Qatar's 0.8, and set there on purpose because the alternative is to imply a force that does not exist. Mauritius has no army, no air force, no navy and no aircraft; the Special Mobile Force is a police reserve with light armour that has been deployed once, to Rodrigues, and the Coast Guard's largest hull in 1990 was an Indian-built patrol vessel. India is the security guarantor by understanding rather than by treaty. A nation with no border, no army and one claim on a country that will not fight it is one the war model can essentially only reach through somebody else, which is the fact.

Claim on the United Kingdom, share 0.00025: the Chagos Archipelago, argued in full on the roster row. Recorded here as the reason a Commonwealth realm carries a live territorial dispute with London: Britain detached the islands in 1965, deported the population, and leased Diego Garcia to the United States, and the base was flying B-52 and KC-135 sorties for the Gulf build-up within the year this game opens.
